rounds.text: Wework India Management Ltd demonstrates exceptional growth and profitability that outpaces the broader market, evidenced by a rules-based screen scoring 78 out of 100 with a buy rating [E53]. The company exhibits robust top-line momentum with compounded sales growth of 23% over 3 years and 27% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15], alongside a strong 3-year compounded profit growth of 36% [E16]. Operational efficiency is exceptionally high, reflected in a towering operating margin of 65% in the TTM period [E19] and an elite return on equity reaching up to 31.6% [E13], easily eclipsing the sector benchmark of 4.77% [E9]. Furthermore, cash generation is extraordinary, highlighted by an operating cash flow of Rs 1,734 Cr fully backing profits with a cash conversion ratio of 23.12x in March 2026 [E23, E24]. Market participants recognize this quality through a phenomenal relative-strength rating of 96 against the Nifty 500 [E41], supported by a powerful sector tailwind score of +0.59 in the services sector [E64]. conceded: [E27], [E35], [E52], [E61].

Wework India Management Ltd trades at an extreme valuation that is fundamentally disconnected from intrinsic value, featuring a price-to-earnings ratio of 105x and a price-to-book ratio of 30.45x [E1, E2]. This lofty multiple is heavily exacerbated by a discounted cash flow model placing intrinsic value at Rs 249 per share against a market price of Rs 670, resulting in a stark margin of safety of -168.8% [E35, E36]. Furthermore, the company carries severe balance sheet and solvency vulnerabilities, highlighted by a debt-to-equity ratio of 18.62x and borrowings surging to Rs 5,550 Cr in March 2026 from just Rs 310 Cr a year earlier [E27, E29]. These liquidity pressures are underscored by a low interest coverage ratio and a dangerously thin current ratio of 0.33x from the prior year [E28, E49]. Adding to the governance and confidence risk, promoters have pledged 35.0% of their holding while cutting their stake by 1.50 percentage points to 48.30% in June 2026, alongside negative institutional money flow and declining foreign institutional ownership [E31, E32, E34, E52]. Conceded: compounded sales growth is 23% over 3 years with an operating margin of 65% in the trailing twelve months, and operating cash flow reached Rs 1,734 Cr in March 2026 [E14, E19, E24].

Conceded: [E1, E2, E35, E36, E27, E29, E28, E49, E31, E32, E34, E52]. While traditional metrics like the DCF flag an overvalued reading, the market price is supported by an exceptional relative-strength rating of 96 against the Nifty 500 and a rules-based screen score of 78 out of 100 [E41, E53]. The operational engine is firing with strong momentum, evidenced by a 27% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months and 28% YoY sales growth on the screen [E15, E54]. Profitability fundamentals remain elite, with a 31.6% return on equity and a robust operating margin of 65% in the TTM [E13, E19]. Furthermore, cash generation is extraordinary; operating cash flow reached Rs 1,734 Cr in March 2026, fully backing profits with a cash conversion of 23.12x [E23, E24]. Finally, the business operates within a verified services sector tailwind with a score of +0.59, where the company's ROCE of 10.83% and sector-beating growth rates easily outpace sector medians [E10, E64, E65, E66, E67].

Conceded: [E41, E53, E15, E54, E13, E19, E23, E24, E64, E65, E66, E67]. While the bull points to strong relative strength and top-line expansion, these metrics completely ignore the massive valuation disconnect where a DCF puts intrinsic value at Rs 249 against a market price of Rs 670, yielding a staggering -168.8% margin of safety [E35, E36]. The reverse DCF further exposes this fragility, showing that today's price demands an unrealistic 31.9% earnings growth compared to the 18.0% base case [E37]. Furthermore, trailing twelve month profit growth has collapsed to -53%, directly contradicting the narrative of unmitigated operating momentum [E17]. This earnings deceleration occurs alongside severe structural vulnerabilities, including a debt-to-equity ratio of 18.62x, borrowings surging to Rs 5,550 Cr, and 35.0% of promoter holdings being pledged [E27, E29, E52]. Finally, institutional confidence is actively eroding through negative money flow and foreign institutional holding declines, signaling that sophisticated capital is fleeing these rich multiples [E32, E34].
